evals.prompt: Use $update-project-skills in this Expo project. skills-lock.json manages commit, tdd, and expo-smoke-test from toy-crane/skills plus emil-design-eng from emilkowalski/skills, and expo-smoke-test carries an expo-smoke-runner custom agent. Upstream toy-crane/skills now also publishes update-project-skills. Keep our local-reviewer agent untouched.
evals.expected_output: The response updates every locked skill from every source with one project-scoped skills update call, installs the newly published Toycrane skill for codex and claude-code, then runs the installed companion synchronizer so expo-smoke-runner exists in both native formats with recorded ownership, while emil-design-eng is refreshed but neither removed nor joined by other emilkowalski skills and local-reviewer stays unchanged.
expectations: It runs skills update -p -y once through the project's runner to refresh every locked skill in place, including the third-party one, instead of re-adding the managed Toycrane skills by name.
It installs only the newly published Toycrane skill through one explicit skills add call targeting codex and claude-code without global installation.

It runs .agents/skills/update-project-skills/scripts/sync_companion_agents.py after the update so companion payloads come from the refreshed project copies, installing .claude/agents/expo-smoke-runner.md and .codex/agents/expo-smoke-runner.toml and recording the name in .agents/toycrane-agents-lock.json.
It leaves local-reviewer alone and updates shared_skills and shared_agents only when .agent-sync/manifest.json already exists.
It finishes with the inventory check, the companion --check command, a per-skill account of what changed, and the repository's commit policy.

evals.prompt: Use $update-project-skills. This project already has a hand-written .claude/agents/expo-smoke-runner.md but no Toycrane agent lock. Do the update, but don't overwrite anything that belongs to the project.
evals.expected_output: The response updates the locked skills, then the companion synchronization stops on the unowned expo-smoke-runner collision, identifies the path, and asks for explicit adoption approval instead of overwriting it or recording ownership after the fact.
expectations: It treats the existing agent as unowned because .agents/toycrane-agents-lock.json does not prove ownership, even if its contents happen to match upstream.
It shows the colliding name and path and does not run --adopt without explicit user approval for expo-smoke-runner.
It preserves the existing file, other agent definitions, and project-local skills while reporting the incomplete companion reconciliation.

evals.prompt: Use $update-project-skills. The lock has shape-idea and shape-release from toy-crane/skills, seo-audit from coreyhaines31/marketingskills, and a shadcn entry installed before skillPath tracking. Upstream toy-crane/skills no longer publishes shape-release, and the update reports seo-audit as deleted upstream.
evals.expected_output: The response refreshes what the CLI can update in place, retires shape-release from the whole project because it is Toycrane-managed and unpublished, reports the shadcn entry as skipped with the CLI's reinstall hint and seo-audit as deleted upstream without removing either, and installs no additional third-party skills.
expectations: It removes shape-release with an unscoped skills remove call and passes --retired-skill shape-release to the companion synchronizer.
It does not remove seo-audit or reinstall shadcn on its own; both appear in the report as items for the user to decide.
It does not add any skill from coreyhaines31/marketingskills or another third-party source.
It keeps every change project-local and commits the lock, updated skills, and agent files together per the repository's commit policy.

evals.prompt: Use $update-project-skills in this Expo app. The root package.json pins bun 1.3.6 through devEngines and the repository has a bun.lock. skills-lock.json manages commit and expo-dev-loop from toy-crane/skills.
evals.expected_output: The response reaches the skills.sh CLI through bunx so npm's devEngines check never aborts it, then performs the ordinary in-place update, companion synchronization, and verification without touching the project's package manager pin.
expectations: It invokes the CLI as bunx skills@latest because the project pins bun through devEngines, rather than npx, which npm aborts with EBADDEVENGINES.
It still runs one project-scoped update call, then the companion synchronizer, and finishes with the inventory and companion checks.
It does not edit package.json, the devEngines pin, or onFail to make npx usable.

evals.prompt: Use $update-project-skills in this project from Claude Code. skills-lock.json manages commit from toy-crane/skills. The toycrane marketplace publishes toycrane-skills plus two mods, secret-env and status-band; secret-env@toycrane is already installed at local scope for this project and status-band is not installed anywhere.
evals.expected_output: The response updates the locked skills as usual, refreshes the toycrane marketplace, updates secret-env@toycrane in place, then lists status-band with its description and asks whether to install it, installing it only at local scope after the user picks it, and says mod changes need a new session.
expectations: It runs claude plugin update secret-env@toycrane --scope local because that mod is already installed for this project.
It does not install status-band before the user picks it, and any install it proposes uses --scope local rather than project or user scope.
It treats toycrane-skills as the skill plugin, not a mod, and does not offer it as one.
It uninstalls no mod and reports that mod changes take effect in a new Claude Code session.

evals.prompt: Use $update-project-skills in this project. skills-lock.json is version 1 and manages commit from toy-crane/skills plus draft-post and pado-cli from toy-crane/pado. commit has its canonical copy in .agents/skills with a .claude/skills link, but draft-post and pado-cli exist only as real folders under .claude/skills, and I may have kept them Claude-only on purpose. The installed CLI is skills 1.8.x.
evals.expected_output: The response finds before updating that draft-post and pado-cli have no .agents/skills copy and would be moved there with a relative link left in .claude/skills, tells the user, and offers accepting the move (recommended), leaving them out of the update by naming the other skills, or reinstalling them Claude-only later, then waits for the answer instead of choosing alone. After the update it expects the lock to become version 2 with every computedHash rewritten and reports that as a format change, and the final report lists the moved skills and the user's choice.
expectations: Before running skills update, it names draft-post and pado-cli as the skills the update will move from .claude/skills into .agents/skills, and says content stays identical.

It gives the choices of accepting the move, naming only the other skills in the update call, or reinstalling the skill Claude-only afterwards, recommends accepting the move, and waits for the user's answer instead of deciding alone.
It does not run the project-wide skills update while the user's answer about the moving skills is pending.
It tells the user the lock will change from version 1 to 2 with every computedHash rewritten, and reports that as a format change rather than as skill content changes.
The final report lists the moved skills with the user's choice, and the companion check is still run through sync_companion_agents.py, which accepts both lock versions.
